web_evidence.title: Gorky Park - Martin Cruz Smith
web_evidence.note: The author’s official site reproduces an early crime-scene passage that calls Arkady “the chief investigator,” repeatedly narrates him as “he,” and reports his thoughts externally.

web_evidence.title: Gorky Park by Martin Cruz Smith | Literature and Writing | Research Starters
web_evidence.note: Whole-book structural analysis identifies Arkady as the narrative lens and discusses his feelings, suspicions, and deductions while consistently treating him as the narrated character; support for third-person limited narration is inferential but extensive.

web_evidence.title: Thrillernik
web_evidence.note: The New York Review of Books reproduces interior narration that presents Arkady as “he” and separately quotes the narrator reporting what “he wonders,” corroborating third-person focalization away from the opening.

web_evidence.title: Books Read in 2015 47. Gorky Park – Martin Cruz Smith

person_note: The controlling narration is third person, chiefly focalized through Arkady Renko. Dispersed quote evidence shows Arkady and other focal characters narrated externally, while the author-site excerpt independently displays the same construction and interior review passages confirm it beyond the opening. Visible first-person and second-person forms occur in character speech or generic maxims, not autonomous narrative sections. q02574 appears to be third-person free-indirect narration despite its upstream dialogue bucket. The main limitation is that the authorized excerpt covers only the opening, but whole-book structural and explicit POV sources agree and targeted searches found no frame, epistolary structure, or sustained person alternation.
